# dsh-xcode-mcp
**English** | 中文
**Apple Xcode MCP bridge for DeepSeek Harness.**

Xcode 27 ships a *headless MCP tool service*. `/usr/bin/xcrun mcpbridge` is the
STDIO bridge to it.

This bundle wires that bridge into the MCP client already
shipped with DeepSeek Harness, so every Xc

ode tool reaches the model as an
ordinary native tool named `mcp__xcode__<ToolName>`.

On Xcode 27.0 that is **54 tools**: project and scheme inspection, builds,
tests, SwiftUI Preview re

ndering, simulator launch and interaction
(tap / type / swipe), screenshots, the accessibility hiera

rchy, OSLog, and
Swift package, localization and instrumentation helpers.
## Why a bundle

Hand-wiring `xcrun mcpbridge` means editing the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and
remembering the tra

nsport fields, the tool-call timeout and the failure policy.
This package carries that configuration

instead, so the connection becomes one
installable thing that is named, versioned, listed in the Pl

ugins page and
removable like any other plugin.

## Requirements

- **macOS**, **Xcode 27 or later**. `mcpbridge` does not exist in earlier
versions.

ervice enabled and running:

On first connection Xcode shows an agent-authorization prompt. A **signed**
client such as DeepSeek

Harness is remembered permanently; an unsigned client's
grant expires after about 24 hours.
## Install
From the **Plugins** page in the sidebar, enter the package name:

Installing enables the bundle; it usually activates through HMR. If the
`mcp__xcode__*` tools do not

appear, restart the profile so the new bundle layer
is composed.
An absolute path to a checkout works the same way, for a pre-publish install.
## Verify

Ask for something that needs Xcode, or check the tool list for `mcp__xcode__*`.
A good first call is
`mcp__xcode__XcodeListWorkspaces`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then `mcp__xcode__XcodeListSchemes` with that identifier lists the project's
schemes. Both were veri
fied against Xcode 27.0 (27A266a).
## Upgrading

**DSH does not update installed plugins automatically.** Its own Plugins page
says so, and re-instal

ling over an existing copy is refused with *"this plugin is
already installed"* — the uninstall is w
hat makes the upgrade possible.
So the Plugins-page route is: **uninstall, then install again.**
From a shell, the same upgrade without the uninstall step:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

One thing to expect either way: the plugin manager installs through pnpm, whose
`minimumReleaseAge`

defaults to `1440`
minutes. **A release less than a day old will not install**, and the command
repo

rts `Already up to date` even though a newer version exists. That is
supply-chain protection, not a

failure — wait a day, or lower the setting in the
profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` if you know the re

a day, or lower the setting in the
profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` if you know the release is yours.

Because this bundle is configuration only, an upgrade replaces a handful of
declaration files. It ru
ns no code before or after.
## Configure

The row is `mcp-xcode`; its `config` is the full
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`
schema, so any field

documented there works. To change one, override the row in
the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` — a

matching override replaces the whole
`config`, so restate every field you still want:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

To point at a specific Xcode instead of the one `xcode-select` names, add `env`
with `MCP_XCODE_PID`

o point at a specific Xcode instead of the one `xcode-select` names, add `env`
with `MCP_XCODE_PID`.
### A note on the 54 tools

Every tool's JSON Schema is offered to the model each turn. If that is more
context than you want, `

@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` has no include/exclude
filter — the alternative is a bridge that implem

-ai/dsh-mcp-client` has no include/exclude
filter — the alternative is a bridge that implements one.
## Remove

Through the Plugins page, or by removing the bundle from `dsh.profile.bundles`
and uninstalling the

package. Disabling the bundle stops the `mcpbridge`
subprocess with it.
